Perfect RPG game! Even the Vanilla version is so immersive. Has so much more potential with updates and developing. Glad the team is still investing in this game. I would throw tons of money at this game.

This game is hard. It can be pretty unforgiving, even on the easier settings. But it's worth it. Tense tactical battles make up the core of the game with party management and other RPG elements woven in smoothly.

This is an unforgiving game. You play as a group of mercs - normal, regular people - trying to thrive in an unforgiving world, full of threats, normal and magic and bigger and stronger than you.

You will be frustrated. It's a steep learning curve. But if you push forward you will love it. It's a great game where you see your men and are proud of their achievements, where a cripple can kill noblemen, have some drinks with his buddies and live to see another day.

I have over 500 hours in this game and sometimes still feel like a newbie. And I keep logging in.

I love this game. it's like tactics ogre meets mount and blade though the story is minimal. You run a merc in a chess like grid. Yo uhad to feed them, arm them, and look for jobs to make money. Fight for nobles. save the townsfolk etc.

Absolutely one of my favorite turn-based tactical games. Took me a long time to pick it up because the art style bugged me, but I've discovered that once you get into the game it grows on you pretty quickly.

Combat is fun, tactical, and allows for some of the best representation of small-troop medieval combat I've seen in a game yet. As someone who does HEMA as a hobby, it's refreshing to play something that actually reflects my experiences in actual armored combat.

While the DLCs aren't mandatory, I'd say they are highly recommended to fully enjoy the game. Especially the Warriors of the North, as the various new starting options really add to the replayability.

Do note that it is a *hard* game, and definitely designed to be played with a tolerance towards losses and failures. If you go into this wanting to win every battle and lose no guys, you might be in for a rough time.

I really enjoyed Battle Brothers.

The mechanics of the game can be summarized as a turn-based mount and blade, in that you form a group of mercenaries and travel around the countryside doing jobs, including escorting caravens and fighting orcs/undead/bandits. Managing your food, weapons, and payroll while traveling around the world to fufill your contracts is the overworld game you play between battles. The battles themselves are turn based and tactical, with each characters weapon defining their abilities.

The art is fantastic, especially with regard to how it shows the damage your characters take in fight. The setting is dark and medieval, but with some sparse fantasy thrown in. You wont recruit any mages, but you will fight plenty of zombies.

Your mercenary company is smaller and more intimate than in M&B, and you get to know your men well. Their deaths, or even grevious injuries, are major events that will leave you grieving.

Also, the game is brutally hard. I would recomend this game to anyone who enjoys punishing tactical games like XCOM or Darkest Dungeon. I have come no where close to beating it, but even the failures make for an enjoyable experience.

All in all, its a great game that is well worth the price.

The devs just dropped an unannounced patch with not only fixes, but real content, after having moved on to other projects. Insert default "THIS IS HOW YOU DO IT, TRIPLE-A STUDIOS!" comment here.

The only downside is a brief period of mod incompatability, but that's not really an issue. I only mention this because mods is what takes this game from good to great to legendary. From 20hrs to 200hrs to 2000hrs.

It achieves that fine balance between simplicity and complexity in several areas: gameplay meta and progression, as well as graphical fidelity. Not even joking. If this game had "better" 3D graphics it would automatically be a worse game. If you play this or Starsector for example, you know what I mean.

Anyway, just buy it, mod it, play it forever.

Ultra punishing and absurdly RNG based sometimes, suggest you save scum unless you love suffering. Ignoring the ultra low chance of instant death on the hedge knight you just spent $10k on, this game is as absurdly fun as it is difficult. The devs have made an absolute masterpiece, and there's a couple of overhaul mods that freshen up the game. I hope that MENACE ends up half as good as Battle Brothers :)

If there was ever a game to unseat X-Com for the amount of frustration you can feel when losing a mercenary/unit, it would be this one. In fact, it totally is.

Get in, get frustrated, and learn how important it is to maintain a formation the hard way.

Only Con for me: No language support other than English.

For being a Germanic folklore inspired game, it would be cool to play it in German.

This is a really fun game. You and your band of mercenaries travel around a gritty low-fantasy world, killing people and monsters for money. The best part is the combat system. It is D20-based, with lots of modifiers for positioning, skills, and terrain to take advantage of. It takes many hours of play to understand in detail, and hundreds of hours to really master.

I quite like it. Haven't played the expansions a whole lot, but the base game and mods are a lot of fun. Most mods require that you have purchased DLCs, so keep that in mind. Its sort of like a mix between Mount and Blade and Darkest Dungeoun

I really enjoy playing this game. I like turn-based tactical games, and Battle Brothers masters the tactical part of it: get the tactics wrong and you lose. So part of the enjoyment is trying to optimize your tactics. 

There's also a great sense of discovery, although there is too much re-use of names, locations, and contracts in the base game. Expansion packs help with this, and I imagine mods do as well, although I haven't explored those yet. 

The overall tone is a little grim, and I hope their next game has a bit more lightheartedness to balance the angst of existing in the world that they created. 

If you're ok embracing a "losing is fun" attitude, and you like to experiment with tactical refinements, this game is for you.

Really fun game, but...
The only problem is there are so many anti-tactical things that stop you from being able to plan. "If bad luck makes your plan fail it wasn't a good plan" How am I meant to make a plan when I have no idea on the terrain, very limited troop placement, inconsistent enemies and task difficulties and vague mechanics. It's a shame because it's a really fun game and I would recommend it but the steep learning curve also comes with a frustrating realisation that the game is more shallow that you think it will be.

It's a great game very fun and if you play it enough that it starts to feel repetitive there are mods on nexus that will introduce new things to the game like a variety of different weapons and adds even harder difficulty to the game.
10/10

I've been enjoing this game for years and still not done with it.

So I wasn't sure what to expect. The game play was difficult at first to learn. There wasn't much in the way of information on strategy, especially for resource management, combat, band composition, etc. But....., as I played I figured a lot of it out as I went. Definitely need to play on beginner mode to start off. the only down side I've seen so far is the repetitive nature of the play and missions. I wish the map was much larger and provided much more in depth game play. It's a little limited in that regard.
It's very terrifying to play but it is very enjoyable. I don't want to lose my brothers!
Most replayable game I've ever played. Fantastic balance and variety, emergent storytelling, tortuous challenges and exciting power scaling.

Fantastic game. Hours upon hours of content. Pretty unique I'd say too I'd say in originality of design, concept and gameplay.

As time goes on you'll get attached to your characters and even level them up to absurd degrees. Of course - an elite farmer was still originally... a farmer so pick who you hire (and treat as expendable) carefully.

The game really can be summarized as Medieval Merc Boss Sim Lite in some ways. You aren't overwhelmed with micromanaging characters or duties or whatnot but you will find yourself carefully curating your company and making sure everything is in order in health, finances, food, gear, weaponry etc. Not every contract is feasible either. Sometimes you'll encounter contracts where the offer is incredibly lowballed or simply...out of your league. Other times it puts you, by pure coincidence, into a dangerous situation.

For example, you attack a group of bandits with decent success... but then on the way back you get ambushed by some Orcs. Even if you win ~ your bottom line might be hurt as a result. So not every fight is a good one. Even if you can win.

But this game is really sandbox mostly. The truest thing to an ending being retirement (potentially after defeating a crisis, if you want) or death.

10/10.
If you haven't played this game, you're missing out.
Don't let the simple art style fool you (legs are overrated, anyway), Battle Brothers is a deep and incredibly entertaining tactical RPG, and one of my all-time favorite games!

Slept on this game forever because I hated the art style. Something about it just did not give itself a good first impressions visually. Ended up catching a streamer I often watch do a run through and felt my opinion change the more I looked at it. Ended up giving it a whirl, and its incredibly addictive. My advise for new players is do a run through of the tutorial campaign and then when you feel capable with the game restart and go for easy difficulty but put it on Ironman. This is one of those titles where you want to feel the highs and lows, if you save scum everytime a character dies you'll never feel the same attachment or the same satisfaction when you bounce back from a low point in your run. It really is the factor that turns this from a capable turn based strategy game into something you'll likely remember for years to come.

Battle Brothers is without a doubt one of the best games I have ever played. The combat, while challenging is fair and is well built to allow strategizing. I honestly can't explain why but every run feels different despite the gameplay and goals always remaining the same. The fact that I've willing gave 800 hours of my life to this game should say something.

Two side notes. The game plays perfectly on the Steam Deck. No problems what so ever. And it barely drains the battery life. I can play for 6 hours strait before needing to charge it. Add to that the variety of mods and you have one of the best games ever on your hands. I bet when I'm on my death bed that I'll still have a company smashing some brigand skulls.

Love it. My only problem was the tutorial, it's hard. I died in my first battle and there was very little instructions. I have clue why the devs did that. It made me want to quit immediately. Tutorials should be easy and with lots of instructions, this was the opposite.

Getting past that, the game is hard, there's no easy mod, even easy mod isn't easy. I had to restart 3 times before I made any real progress. Again very frustrating, but I'm glad I didn't quit. The game is amazing. "save game" is your best friend :)

This has been on of the best valued games i've EVER played. With so much replayability and unique mechanics. The music is great. Sound effects are spot on. The vast majority of equipment, skills, units and different "contracts" are stunning. You can tell the Devs put ALOT of love and work dedication into this game and the price is phenomonal well suited. Lots of enemies with different behavior patterns and abilities mean you have to make tough choices and decide how versatile you need to be for success. High replayability. 5/5

This game is very simple, and this simplicity makes it great. Each game has a different map, and more or less different events. The best of this game is that I played it in short time spans during many years. You can play a bit forget about it some days and easily continue later.

If you only want to have some fun with a tactic game, it is a great option.

After reading a lot of seemingly enthusiastic comments I am rather disappointed with what the game actually has to offer. It is not very deep, it is not very convincing and it is very repetitive. Even tactical battles seem somehow unrewarding and do not give you a feeling of tactical sophistication. I could write pages about what might be done better in this game, starting from the poor UI which often makes battles difficult to read. But I will save your time with this conclusion: Utruk the Desolation is a much better game in all aspects, although not accompanied by such a hype. Buy that instead.

The best turn based strategy ever. Well balanced (not kidding), amazing visual, very atmosphere music, tons of content, variative gameplay. Actually this game is for hundreds and hundreds hours, every try - new adventure with new experience and new challenges. Absolutely recommended.

I have played it for way too little to know about its full potential, but in my experience, with games like these, you can get the idea of whether it's going to be good or bad after the first few minutes.

What struck me the most is the fact that I actually enjoyed it, which is a rare thing for me to experience with games nowadays. Perhaps it's because it has the things I look for in games - proper leveling/skill tree system, quests, lore-rich quests, strategy, great trading system, and most of all...

There's so much this game has done well. The soundtrack, the combat/map gameplay loop, the character customization, and the writing. You actually feel like your resolving problems that occur in the world, and you see effects done to settlements from your actions almost right away. You see a settlement that has a problem with missing children? There's probably a contract for the witch that's stealing them. It's too bad the world sim doesn't go any deeper than this, but I'd say it's just enough to keep the experience of being dirty, bloody sellswords pretty alive and meaningful.

The writing kind of makes you feel like your dirty bloody and murderous sometimes, though. Everyone hates you, and eventually you sort of just accept it. It kind of makes you feel like a group of Witchers or monsters in a way sometimes.

You can play as a solo hero/monster hunter, a ragtag mess of mercenaries, or the brothers just trying to get by... evidently, you can also play as a trader and explorer too. This game is definitely in my top 6.
